extracted.intended_audience: Army commanders, public affairs officers (PAOs), installation public affairs staff, and other Army personnel responsible for public information/media relations
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for Army public affairs activities, media relations, and release of official information (including press releases, photography, media access, and sensitive-case procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of electronic mail and Internet
rubrics_metrics.description: Using electronic mail and the Internet are alternative means of immediate information access. Both provide an avenue for timely feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internet and Intranet allow the commander to further increase the distribution of print and broadcast mediums to reach a wider audience. Creators and designers of this material will ensure that it meets OPSEC requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and evaluate audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: The PAOs will assess and evaluate all audiences to develop a sound PA program through sensing sessions, focus groups, surveys, or interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders must be aware of all the subgroups in their commands; each has unique information needs (examples: first-term Soldiers, junior NCOs, senior NCOs, company grade officers, field grade officers, spouses, children, civilian employees, ROTC cadets, RC Soldiers, retirees, local nationals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with state and local officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Presidential, DOD, and HQDA policies require that, within national security and congressional constraints, state and local officials be consulted at the earliest stages of planning and developing major policy, budget, or reorganization proposals that have significant state and local impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCPA will provide consultation guidance to the ASCC, ACOM, or DRU and activities involved. No early consultation with state/local officials will take place without HQDA guidance. Commands should advise HQDA OCPA and OCLL of local issues via the local PAO and congressional affairs contact officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization and limits for visual information support
rubrics_metrics.description: Official photography, television, audio, and graphic art support to public information programs is authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording and reproducing is kept to the minimum required to satisfy official needs; photographic and video coverage of VIP visits is restricted to minimum essential requirements; PA resources may produce limited documentation for Soldiers (farewell books, slideshows, videos) when not interfering with primary mission; PA authorized to take news-related photographs only — using PA resources for non-newsworthy social events is inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitating media visits
rubrics_metrics.description: News media representatives may visit areas normally open to the public when subject matter is of local interest or deals with unplanned news events and information is releasable under existing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access is restricted where criminal-justice control is required. Coverage of potentially controversial or national-level subjects must be coordinated through channels to OCPA for review/approval. Installations/contractors will cooperate timely with bona fide media requests. Local procedures should handle media during disasters or civil disturbances. Basic ground rules should ensure free flow of information while safeguarding classified materials. Under no circumstances will PA personnel use physical force against media; OCPA is sole authority to approve foreign media visits in CONUS (with limited exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: News media accreditation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Accreditation identifies correspondents with a legitimate need for gathering news about military affairs and fosters a professional relationship between the military and the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accreditation does not provide special privileges; accessing areas, receiving information, and using facilities remain commander prerogatives. OASD(PA) establishes accreditation criteria for combat coverage; commanders may establish local accreditation systems for events. Staff privileges/credentials: PAOs issue credentials for AF/CE publications staff reporters; contractors should carry printer/contractor credentials; Stars and Stripes reporters receive credentials as civilian media; military journalists afforded same rights as civilian media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media day encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year commanders of active installations should schedule a media day to encourage area news media representatives to visit and establish or renew contacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program type and date at commander discretion; media days should be conducted with scheduled on-post special events and/or ongoing training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official discussions with the media
rubrics_metrics.description: Army personnel are encouraged to speak with the media factually, candidly, and fully about unclassified matters on which they have personal knowledge and expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior commanders and staff officers are expected to discuss military matters within their purview with news media representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unofficial discussions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone subject to this regulation may agree to a media request for an interview in an unofficial capacity and may express personal opinions unless limited by law or regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should discuss candidly matters about which they have personal knowledge if information is not classified or otherwise nonreleasable. When questioned on a classified matter, they must state that the information cannot be discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of unclassified official visual information to foreign nationals
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedures and policies on release of information to U.S. media, organizations, or individuals also apply to official visual information material released to foreign nationals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests of unusual or sensitive nature should be referred to OCPA for coordination/approval. Requests from foreign governments should be referred to the nearest security manager per AR 380–10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal privacy and the Privacy Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The Privacy Act of 1974 generally prohibits the Department of the Army from publicly releasing certain items of information about an individual without that individual's consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented by AR 340–21; PAOs must follow Privacy Act constraints when releasing personal information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of information on disciplinary actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on release of information on disciplinary actions is provided in AR 25–55.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal investigation and polygraph activities guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: See AR 195–6, paragraph 2–9, for guidance on criminal investigations and Department of the Army polygraph activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of information from criminal investigation and MP records
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on release of information from criminal investigation and military police records, reports, and forms is in AR 190–45, AR 195–2, and AR 340–21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military accidents: cooperation and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with national security, military authorities will give maximum cooperation to U.S. news representatives covering military accidents occurring outside military installations, except for accidents involving NBC weapons/research or incidents OCONUS where other laws/treaties apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate and plan with civilian law enforcement/emergency agencies before a crisis; advise agencies of potential assistance. Civilian agencies should be made aware of relevant USC sections criminalizing photographing or publishing classified information. At scenes with exposed classified material: inform media, request cooperation in protection; do not use force; request civilian law enforcement assistance to recover materials and report refusals through channels to OCPA/OASD(PA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accident reporting format and withholding names until next of kin notified
rubrics_metrics.description: When circumstances permit, one-story, single-release coverage of accidents or incidents is desirable. Normally the initial information will include announcement that an accident occurred, location and time, and withheld names/addresses of deceased or injured until next of kin have been officially notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After notification, PAO may release names and city/state addresses. Avoid statements inviting speculation; release names simultaneously with accident news when possible. Civilian aircraft under military charter considered military aircraft. Coordinate with local law enforcement and transportation company reps to ensure next of kin notified prior to public release when accidents occur outside Army installations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval levels for high-profile casualty releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific approval authorities are required for releasing casualty information on key U.S. Government personnel or equivalently ranked foreign government visitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White House Press Secretary has sole approval for President, Vice President, Speaker, President Pro Tempore, Cabinet members, and equivalent foreign visitors. Secretary of Defense (Public Affairs) approves releases about Senators, Representatives, Service Secretaries, CJCS, Service Chiefs, Commandants, and specified commanders. Commanders handle special-interest personnel per AR 600–8–1. Local PAOs may release information on named individuals prior to notifying OCPA but must immediately notify OCPA after release. OCONUS accidents require coordination with Embassy/Consulate. Names of special operations personnel coordinated with USASOC prior to release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-release of information from official investigations without approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Information resulting from official investigations regarding line-of-duty status or findings of misconduct by individuals will not be released to the public without specified HQDA approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval required from The Adjutant General, HQDA for USAR/retired Army members, or HQDA (DAPC–PED) for AA members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casualty terminology guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using the term 'casualty' in news releases when referring to military personnel; instead identify personnel as deceased, very seriously wounded/injured/ill, seriously wounded/injured/ill, slightly wounded/injured/ill, or missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate cause for deceased and wounded/ill categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Armed Forces Disciplinary Control Board meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: News media representatives may attend those meetings of Armed Forces Disciplinary Control Boards that are open to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See AR 190–24, appendix B, for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews and hometown-type releases for foreign military students
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs will not initiate interviews with foreign military personnel attending Army schools or training under Army auspices in the U.S.; interview requests referred to the student's senior officer in residence for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The senior officer should consult the embassy's desires. If approved, PAO will help arrange. U.S. Army and Air Force Hometown News Service will not release news regarding foreign military personnel; it releases news only on U.S. personnel to U.S. media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterintelligence information release coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Public release of information about U.S. Army counterintelligence personnel or activities must be coordinated in advance with the Deputy Chief of Staff, G–2, per AR 381–20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical facility patient information release restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about patients under treatment in Army medical facilities will be released only in accordance with FOIA, the Privacy Act of 1974, and HIPAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biographical data other than that releasable under AR 340–21 and Protected Health Information will not be released without prior consent recorded on DA Form 4876. In response to media queries, permitted items include admission/release dates, general injury/disease type (avoid speculation), description of patient's specific condition only with written consent, a current assessment limited to 'stable (or good, fair, serious, or critical)' — prognosis never given. For non-Army Service patients in Army facilities, release authority rests with the other Service/agency unless official request and policy permit. Photographing or permitting interviews with psychiatric/other mental patients is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing in action / whereabouts unknown restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Names and addresses of next of kin or photographs/videos of a person MIA or whereabouts unknown will not be released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name, grade, DOB, a statement of status, and other proper info may be released only after verification that next of kin were officially notified and search-and-rescue operations terminated. Details about escape/return, physical condition, scheduled return, or information provided by returnees about others will not be released until next of kin have been notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on release for personnel in alcohol/drug programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Public release of information regarding personnel who are or were participating in Army alcohol and drug abuse control programs is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation and debarment information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: To preclude premature release, PAOs must maintain a close liaison with the SJA on litigation and debarment cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters in litigation or with litigation potential will not be discussed unless information is public record; PAO and SJA will coordinate responses; PAOs will never speculate. Debarment information not released until final decision; interim acknowledgement that a company has been proposed for debarment is permitted, but refer media to contractor for basis/status questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of courts-martial photography/video rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Approving news media requests to photograph or video record a trial by court-martial guided by measures necessary to ensure a fair trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographing/videoing courtroom interior may be permitted when persons involved are not present. During trial, photographing/videoing the accused may be permitted when outdoors in public view; photographing within courtroom, cell, cell block, prison yard, or in presence of other prisoners is not permitted. PAO will establish means to accommodate media coverage, including courtroom pool reporting and a separate media center near the courtroom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording Soldiers: accurate portrayal
rubrics_metrics.description: When releasing visual information documentation of Soldiers, PAOs will ensure accurate portrayal in situations reflecting Army activities, missions, and uniforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographing and recording personnel in hostile areas — protections and prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Care will be taken when releasing official information, photographs, and video recordings of U.S. and allied forces personnel killed, wounded, hospitalized, detained, or MIA; consider rights of individuals and effects on families and friends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use common sense, good taste, and awareness of safety/security when authorizing media access. If photographers persist in taking prohibited photos, PAO should report through channels rather than attempt to recover film. Prohibited official release without permission (unless notation of permission placed): (1) photos/video of recognizable wounded or deceased not identified by name; (2) recognizable wounded identified by name until next of kin notified (unless release approved by wounded person); (3) surgical/major medical care photos identifying patient; (4) photos/video showing deceased and/or wounded in large numbers; (5) photos/video showing mangled bodies, obvious agony, or severe shock; (6) photos/video of psychiatric or other mental patients; (7) photos/video of plastic surgery or severe disfigurement cases; (8) photos/video of blind or deaf patients; (9) photos/video of amputees demonstrating prosthetic appliances. Official combat-deceased photos under field conditions normally will not be released; photographing graves registration facilities or temporary cemeteries is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official photography/recording in medical facilities consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Permission to photograph or record a patient in a U.S. Army medical facility will be given only when prior informed written consent of the patient has been obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attending physician and/or medical facility commander must determine such activity will not jeopardize patient or nearby patients. Photographing prohibited when it infringes on privacy or causes embarrassment; photographing must meet accepted standards of propriety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographing military installations or equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Public access to Army installations is determined by local commands; photographing historical buildings/areas of public interest for private use generally permitted but subject to local approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground or aerial photographs, sketches, or graphic representations of classified military equipment or installations designated as restricted areas is punishable by law (18 USC 795). Reproducing, publishing, or selling such material is punishable unless the item indicates it has been reviewed and cleared for release by proper authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premature release of Army studies prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Premature release of emerging results of Army studies and/or analyses before official approval is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposing forces (OPFOR) public information policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on policy for releasing public information on OPFOR equipment and training and for public displays/demonstrations is contained in AR 350–2, para 2–7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media coverage of equipment testing prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Media coverage of developmental, technological validation, or operational testing of Army systems is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception to policy only through channels to the OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Battle labs and advanced warfighting experiments coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Major ACOM-level approval may be given for media coverage of Army battle labs and warfighting experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such coverage must be in coordination with OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activation, inactivation, realignment announcement criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurate and timely information, consistent with security and AR 5–10 policies, will be released to the public when decision made to activate, inactivate, or realign installations/facilities/activities and/or associated personnel reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for initial announcements made at HQDA level through OSD when action (1) requires prior notification of Congress per AR 5–10 para 3–4 because of personnel reductions, (2) involves reductions due to commercial activity actions, (3) involves accessing Government installations/facilities, or (4) has generated congressional/public interest or controversy. CPA may make exceptions on release level; CPA will issue guidance prior to scheduled announcement; personnel should avoid statements that invite speculation; commanders will implement procedures for public feedback on realignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit activations/inactivations/reorganizations release rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial release on activations/inactivations/reorganizations of AA units brigade or larger normally at national level; smaller AA units may be announced by ASCC/ACOM/DRU except when criteria in 5–38 apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain safeguarded information generally not releasable on any phase of activation/inactivation/reorganization/training/movements: (1) exact personnel strength and composition; (2) status, amounts, or quality of equipment; (3) combat efficiency; (4) deployment of units to combat areas. For RC units: USAR local commander may release info in b(1)–(3); ARNG state adjutant general may release local unit info after NGB notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and movement information release limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on unit training or movement that is not safeguarded may be released by the responsible commander, except in cases of major or Joint exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial release of information on major Army exercises will be made at HQDA through OSD; initial release on major Joint exercises will be made by OSD with later Joint commander announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination for visits to MEPS and commissaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to Military Entrance Processing Stations covered by joint service regulation guidance; requests to visit commissary facilities must be coordinated with the PA office of the Defense Commissary Agency, Fort Lee, VA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See AR 601–270 para 3–12 for MEPS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visits to installations with NBC or defense-related missions
rubrics_metrics.description: All news media requests to cover NBC missions or activities considered case-by-case and normally approved by the chemical activity or installation commander when such visits will not interfere with operational requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval may be denied for safety or security reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Army confinement facilities normally prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: News media access to and photography in an Army confinement facility normally is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See AR 190–47 para 10–12 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal investigations information release coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, no information should be released concerning ongoing investigations without close coordination with local authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs may acknowledge the existence of an investigation after coordination and any information released cannot violate the Privacy Act or impede an ongoing investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspector General records and release authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspector General (IG) records are privileged documents containing sensitive information and advice; unauthorized use or release can compromise IG effectiveness and confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated release authority for all IG records is The Inspector General. See AR 20–1, chap 3 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army support to disaster relief and civil disturbances — information release and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on Army participation in disaster relief operations will be made available promptly to news media; PAOs should forward news/feature material of activities to OCPA for possible national dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon conclusion of disaster relief activities, PAOs will provide OCPA a narrative summary of PA activities and results; provide information copies to intermediate headquarters. OCPA responsible for PA activities related to civil disturbances; ARNG and USAR PAOs forward questions to OCPA or respective PA offices as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of information by contractors, manufacturers, researchers and other commercial entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Army review and clearance applies to materials proposed for public release by contractors, manufacturers, researchers, and other entities regarding contractual agreements, awards, products, services, military sales, technology, scientific studies, and related areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army policy is to make available maximum accurate information on contractual relationships, industry accomplishments, and scientific achievements. Exceptions include (1) safeguarded information or data that offers unfair competitive advantages, (2) nonexportable commercial information or data and information subject to International Traffic in Arms control, and (3) information about material on the Militarily Critical Technologies List (MCTL).
